R2-05 · A new amber bar can show up out of view. How should it be seen?

Today every page's amber bar sits at the top of its page and scrolls away with it. Scrolled down a long page, a new bar shows up above the screen: a screen reader still reads it out, but nobody looking at the screen sees it. The example (Camps → Thanksgiving Camp in the preview): Zoe Park is withdrawn, and her Undo fails (made to fail with the preview's failNextSave). Its bar, "Undo didn't save. Check the connection, then retry.", is 280px above the screen on a PC and 1,295px above it on a phone. Nothing on Zoe's row says so: she just stays under Removed. The same goes for any long page (rosters, lists) and any bar (a failed save or Undo, a refusal). A failed row save is easier to spot, since some rows show "Not saved".

Today

The failed Undo leaves no mark on the screen. The person thinks Zoe is back, or doesn't notice she isn't.

The amber outlines below mark the bar, or the pointer in C.

How should a new amber bar be seen when it shows up out of view?

A · Under the top bar, where the offline bar shows (my pick)

Every page's amber bar shows just under the top bar, above the page: the same place as the one offline bar (v1.123) and Panel size's bar (v1.118). It's in view however far the page is scrolled, and the page stays still as it comes or goes (v1.124, already built for that place). Bars inside an open box or side panel stay inside it.

+ Always seen, at every size, and nothing moves under the finger.
+ One place for every problem, where the offline bar already is.
− Each section's page bars move there. I build the place once in the shared bar, and each section switches its page bars to it (a small change per page).
− On a phone it takes 2 to 4 lines at the top (59px here, 98px at 320 wide) until it's closed or fixed.

B · The page scrolls up to the bar

When a bar shows up out of view, the page scrolls up until the bar is at the top of the screen.

+ Bars stay where they are today: the smallest change.
− The person loses their place: Zoe's row is now below the screen (183px on PC, about 1.4 screens on a phone), and they scroll back down to her.
− The page moves by itself, so a tap aimed while it scrolls can land on something else. That's what v1.124 stopped the offline bar from doing.

C · A small pointer at the top of the page

The bar stays at the top of its page. While it's out of view, a small amber pointer with its first words shows at the top of the page area. Tapping it scrolls up to the bar.

+ The page never moves by itself, and bars stay where they are.
− A new kind of thing on screen, and two places for one problem.
− The pointer covers a little of the page (here part of a row's Check in), and reading the rest of the bar, or pressing Retry, takes a tap and a scroll.

Page 2: A at tablet and 320 wide. After this: leaving the page while an Undo waits (question 4).

A at tablet 820×1180 touch and 320 wide (phone 390 is on page 1)

The same bar under the top bar, lined up with the page's edges; the page stays where it was.
